# NGLE Triangle Voxelization

Also called: N-gle

## Overview
NGLE Triangle Voxelization is a rasterization-based algorithm for converting triangle meshes into a sparse voxel data structure (specifically a Sparse Voxel DAG or Octree) by classifying triangles into nine cases based on the thickness of their axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) in grid coordinates [S1, unofficial]. It efficiently determines which voxels are intersected by a triangle using plane and projection tests [S1, unofficial].

## How it works
**Inputs and Outputs:**
*   **Input:** A list of triangles (each with 3 vertices in world space), a voxel side length `unitlength`, and a partition range defined by `morton_start` and `morton_end` (Morton codes) [S1, unofficial].
*   **Output:** A sparse voxel grid where intersected voxels are marked. In binary mode, a boolean flag is set; in data-rich mode, normal and color data are stored [S1, unofficial].

**Data Structures:**
*   `VoxelData`: A struct containing `normal` (vec3) and `color` (vec3, computed as the average of the three vertex colors). Used only when `BINARY_VOXELIZATION` is not defined [S1, unofficial].
*   `voxels`: An array indexed by Morton code. If `BINARY_VOXELIZATION` is defined, `voxels` is `bool*`; otherwise, it is `size_t*` (indices into a `vector<VoxelData>`) [S1, unofficial].
*   `p_bbox_grid`: The bounding box of the current partition in grid coordinates, with `min` and `max` components [S1, unofficial].

**Parameters:**
*   `unitlength`: The side length of a voxel in world units [S1, unofficial].
*   `morton_start`, `morton_end`: The range of Morton codes allocated for the current partition [S1, unofficial].

**Algorithm Steps:**

1.  **Initialize Voxel Array:** If `BINARY_VOXELIZATION` is defined, allocate `bool* voxels`. Otherwise, allocate `size_t* voxels` and `vector<VoxelData>& voxel_data`. Clear the voxel entries for the range `[morton_start, morton_end)` to `EMPTY_VOXEL` (or `false`) [S1, unofficial].
2.  **Compute Partition Bounding Box:** Decode `morton_start` and `morton_end - 1` into 3D grid coordinates to determine `p_bbox_grid.min` and `p_bbox_grid.max` [S1, unofficial].
3.  **Process Each Triangle:**
    *   **Compute World AABB:** Calculate the world-space bounding box `t_bbox_world` of the triangle vertices [S1, unofficial].
    *   **Convert to Grid AABB:** Convert `t_bbox_world` to grid coordinates `t_bbox_grid` by multiplying by `unit_div` (`1.0f / unitlength`) and casting to `int`. Clamp `t_bbox_grid` to `p_bbox_grid` to stay within the partition [S1, unofficial].
    *   **Determine Thickness:** Compute the `one_thick` vector [S1, unofficial]. For each axis $i \in \{X, Y, Z\}$:
        $$ \text{one\_thick}[i] = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } t\_bbox\_grid.min[i] == t\_bbox\_grid.max[i] \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} $$
    *   **Compute Triangle Geometry:**
        *   Edges: $e_0 = v_1 - v_0$, $e_1 = v_2 - v_1$, $e_2 = v_0 - v_2$.
        *   Normal: $n = \text{normalize}(e_0 \times e_1)$ [S1, unofficial].
    *   **Case Classification and Voxelization:**
        *   **Cases 4-6 (2D Bounding Box):** If $\sum \text{one\_thick} == 1$, the triangle is thin in one axis. Identify the dominant axis (where `one_thick` is 1). Perform a 2D projection test on the plane perpendicular to the dominant axis [S1, unofficial].
            *   **Case 4 (Thin in X, Thick in Y, Z):** Project onto YZ plane [S1, unofficial]. Compute edge normals $n_{yz\_e0} = \text{vec2}(-e_0[Z], e_0[Y])$, etc [S1, unofficial]. If $n[X] < 0$, negate all $n_{yz\_ei}$. Compute offsets $d_{yz\_ei} = -1.0f \cdot (n_{yz\_ei} \cdot \text{vec2}(v_i[Y], v_i[Z])) + \max(0.0f, \text{unitlength} \cdot n_{yz\_ei}[0]) + \max(0.0f, \text{unitlength} \cdot n_{yz\_ei}[1])$ [S1, unofficial]. Iterate $y, z$ in `t_bbox_grid`. Compute Morton index with fixed $x = t\_bbox\_grid.min[X]$ [S1, unofficial]. Test: For point $p_{yz} = \text{vec2}(y, z)$, if $(n_{yz\_ei} \cdot p_{yz} + d_{yz\_ei}) < 0$ for all $i \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, skip [S1, unofficial]. Otherwise, mark voxel [S1, unofficial].
            *   **Case 5 (Thin in Y, Thick in X, Z):** Project onto ZX plane [S1, unofficial]. Compute edge normals $n_{zx\_e0} = \text{vec2}(-e_0[X], e_0[Z])$, etc [S1, unofficial]. If $n[Y] < 0$, negate all $n_{zx\_ei}$. Compute offsets $d_{zx\_ei}$ similarly. Iterate $z, x$ in `t_bbox_grid`. Compute Morton index with fixed $y = t\_bbox\_grid.min[Y]$ [S1, unofficial]. Test projection against all three edges. Mark if intersected [S1, unofficial].
            *   **Case 6 (Thin in Z, Thick in X, Y):** Project onto XY plane [S1, unofficial]. Compute edge normals $n_{xy\_e0} = \text{vec2}(-e_0[Y], e_0[X])$, etc [S1, unofficial]. If $n[Z] < 0$, negate all $n_{xy\_ei}$. Compute offsets $d_{xy\_ei}$ similarly. Iterate $x, y$ in `t_bbox_grid`. Compute Morton index with fixed $z = t\_bbox\_grid.min[Z]$ [S1, unofficial]. Test projection against all three edges. Mark if intersected [S1, unofficial].
        *   **Cases 7-9 (3D Bounding Box):** If $\sum \text{one\_thick} == 0$, the triangle has variable size in all dimensions [S1, unofficial]. Determine the dominant axis of the normal $n$ (the axis with the largest absolute component). Compute critical point $c$:
            $$ c[i] = \begin{cases} \text{unitlength} & \text{if } n[i] > 0 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} $$
            Compute plane distances for the bounding box:
            *   $d_1 = n \cdot (c - v_0)$
            *   $d_2 = n \cdot ((\delta_p - c) - v_0)$, where $\delta_p = \text{vec3}(\text{unitlength}, \text{unitlength}, \text{unitlength})$ [S1, unofficial].
            Setup projection tests for all three planes (XY, YZ, ZX) as in Cases 4-6. Iterate $x, y, z$ in `t_bbox_grid`. Compute Morton index. **Plane Intersection Test:** Let $p = \text{vec3}(x, y, z)$. If $(n \cdot p + d_1) \cdot (n \cdot p + d_2) > 0.0f$, skip. This checks if the voxel center is entirely on one side of the triangle plane (assuming the plane passes through the box, $d_1$ and $d_2$ have opposite signs) [S1, unofficial]. **Projection Tests:** If the plane test passes, test the voxel against all three 2D projection planes. If any projection test fails (voxel is outside the triangle's 2D shadow on that plane), skip. Otherwise, mark voxel [S1, unofficial].

**Pseudocode:**

> **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors.

```python
def voxelize_ngle(triangles, unitlength, morton_start, morton_end, binary_mode=True):
    # 1. Initialize
    voxel_count = morton_end - morton_start
    if binary_mode:
        voxels = [False] * voxel_count
        voxel_data = None
    else:
        voxels = [0] * voxel_count
        voxel_data = []

    unit_div = 1.0 / unitlength
    
    # 2. Compute Partition Bounding Box
    p_min = decode_morton_3d(morton_start)
    p_max = decode_morton_3d(morton_end - 1)
    
    for tri in triangles:
        # 3. Compute Grid AABB
        t_bbox_min = clamp(int(floor(min(tri.v0.x, tri.v1.x, tri.v2.x) * unit_div)), p_min.x, p_max.x)
        t_bbox_max = clamp(int(floor(max(tri.v0.x, tri.v1.x, tri.v2.x) * unit_div)), p_min.x, p_max.x)
        t_bbox_min.y = clamp(int(floor(min(tri.v0.y, tri.v1.y, tri.v2.y) * unit_div)), p_min.y, p_max.y)
        t_bbox_max.y = clamp(int(floor(max(tri.v0.y, tri.v1.y, tri.v2.y) * unit_div)), p_min.y, p_max.y)
        t_bbox_min.z = clamp(int(floor(min(tri.v0.z, tri.v1.z, tri.v2.z) * unit_div)), p_min.z, p_max.z)
        t_bbox_max.z = clamp(int(floor(max(tri.v0.z, tri.v1.z, tri.v2.z) * unit_div)), p_min.z, p_max.z)
        
        # 4. Determine Thickness
        one_thick = [0, 0, 0]
        for axis in range(3):
            if t_bbox_min[axis] == t_bbox_max[axis]:
                one_thick[axis] = 1
        
        # 5. Compute Geometry
        e0 = tri.v1 - tri.v0
        e1 = tri.v2 - tri.v1
        e2 = tri.v0 - tri.v2
        n = normalize(cross(e0, e1))
        
        sum_one_thick = sum(one_thick)
        
        if sum_one_thick == 1:
            # Cases 4-6: 2D Projection
            dominant_axis = one_thick.index(1)
            
            if dominant_axis == 0: # Case 4: Thin X, Project YZ
                for z in range(t_bbox_min.z, t_bbox_max.z + 1):
                    for y in range(t_bbox_min.y, t_bbox_max.y + 1):
                        p_2d = vec2(y, z)
                        if test_2d_proj(p_2d, tri, unitlength, axis=0):
                            morton = encode_morton_3d(t_bbox_min.x, y, z)
                            voxels[morton - morton_start] = True if binary_mode else add_voxel_data(voxels, voxel_data, tri, morton)
                            
            elif dominant_axis == 1: # Case 5: Thin Y, Project ZX
                for x in range(t_bbox_min.x, t_bbox_max.x + 1):
                    for z in range(t_bbox_min.z, t_bbox_max.z + 1):
                        p_2d = vec2(z, x)
                        if test_2d_proj(p_2d, tri, unitlength, axis=1):
                            morton = encode_morton_3d(x, t_bbox_min.y, z)
                            voxels[morton - morton_start] = True if binary_mode else add_voxel_data(voxels, voxel_data, tri, morton)
                            
            elif dominant_axis == 2: # Case 6: Thin Z, Project XY
                for y in range(t_bbox_min.y, t_bbox_max.y + 1):
                    for x in range(t_bbox_min.x, t_bbox_max.x + 1):
                        p_2d = vec2(x, y)
                        if test_2d_proj(p_2d, tri, unitlength, axis=2):
                            morton = encode_morton_3d(x, y, t_bbox_min.z)
                            voxels[morton - morton_start] = True if binary_mode else add_voxel_data(voxels, voxel_data, tri, morton)
                            
        elif sum_one_thick == 0:
            # Cases 7-9: 3D Bounding Box
            abs_n = abs(n)
            dominant_axis = argmax(abs_n)
            
            c = vec3(0.0)
            for axis in range(3):
                if n[axis] > 0:
                    c[axis] = unitlength
            
            delta_p = vec3(unitlength, unitlength, unitlength)
            d1 = dot(n, c - tri.v0)
            d2 = dot(n, (delta_p - c) - tri.v0)
            
            for z in range(t_bbox_min.z, t_bbox_max.z + 1):
                for y in range(t_bbox_min.y, t_bbox_max.y + 1):
                    for x in range(t_bbox_min.x, t_bbox_max.x + 1):
                        p = vec3(x, y, z)
                        
                        # Plane Intersection Test
                        val = dot(n, p) + d1
                        val2 = dot(n, p) + d2
                        if val * val2 > 0.0:
                            continue
                            
                        # Projection Tests
                        p_xy = vec2(x, y)
                        p_yz = vec2(y, z)
                        p_zx = vec2(z, x)
                        
                        if (test_2d_proj(p_xy, tri, unitlength, axis=2) and
                            test_2d_proj(p_yz, tri, unitlength, axis=0) and
                            test_2d_proj(p_zx, tri, unitlength, axis=1)):
                            
                            morton = encode_morton_3d(x, y, z)
                            voxels[morton - morton_start] = True if binary_mode else add_voxel_data(voxels, voxel_data, tri, morton)

def test_2d_proj(p_2d, tri, unitlength, axis):
    e0 = tri.v1 - tri.v0
    e1 = tri.v2 - tri.v1
    e2 = tri.v0 - tri.v2
    n = normalize(cross(e0, e1))
    
    if axis == 0: # YZ plane
        n_e0 = vec2(-e0.z, e0.y)
        n_e1 = vec2(-e1.z, e1.y)
        n_e2 = vec2(-e2.z, e2.y)
        if n.x < 0:
            n_e0 = -n_e0; n_e1 = -n_e1; n_e2 = -n_e2
        d0 = -dot(n_e0, vec2(tri.v0.y, tri.v0.z)) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e0.x) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e0.y)
        d1 = -dot(n_e1, vec2(tri.v1.y, tri.v1.z)) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e1.x) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e1.y)
        d2 = -dot(n_e2, vec2(tri.v2.y, tri.v2.z)) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e2.x) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e2.y)
    elif axis == 1: # ZX plane
        n_e0 = vec2(-e0.x, e0.z)
        n_e1 = vec2(-e1.x, e1.z)
        n_e2 = vec2(-e2.x, e2.z)
        if n.y < 0:
            n_e0 = -n_e0; n_e1 = -n_e1; n_e2 = -n_e2
        d0 = -dot(n_e0, vec2(tri.v0.z, tri.v0.x)) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e0.x) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e0.y)
        d1 = -dot(n_e1, vec2(tri.v1.z, tri.v1.x)) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e1.x) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e1.y)
        d2 = -dot(n_e2, vec2(tri.v2.z, tri.v2.x)) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e2.x) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e2.y)
    else: # XY plane
        n_e0 = vec2(-e0.y, e0.x)
        n_e1 = vec2(-e1.y, e1.x)
        n_e2 = vec2(-e2.y, e2.x)
        if n.z < 0:
            n_e0 = -n_e0; n_e1 = -n_e1; n_e2 = -n_e2
        d0 = -dot(n_e0, vec2(tri.v0.x, tri.v0.y)) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e0.x) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e0.y)
        d1 = -dot(n_e1, vec2(tri.v1.x, tri.v1.y)) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e1.x) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e1.y)
        d2 = -dot(n_e2, vec2(tri.v2.x, tri.v2.y)) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e2.x) + max(0.0, unitlength * n_e2.y)
        
    if dot(n_e0, p_2d) + d0 < 0: return False
    if dot(n_e1, p_2d) + d1 < 0: return False
    if dot(n_e2, p_2d) + d2 < 0: return False
    return True

def add_voxel_data(voxels, voxel_data, tri, morton):
    normal = normalize(cross(tri.v1 - tri.v0, tri.v2 - tri.v1))
    color = (tri.v0_color + tri.v1_color + tri.v2_color) / 3.0
    voxel_data.append(VoxelData(morton, normal, color))
    return len(voxel_data) - 1

# Standard Morton encoding/decoding [G]
def encode_morton_3d(x, y, z):
    m = 0
    for i in range(10):
        m |= (x & (1 << i)) << (2 * i)
        m |= (y & (1 << i)) << (2 * i + 1)
        m |= (z & (1 << i)) << (2 * i + 2)
    return m

def decode_morton_3d(m):
    x = y = z = 0
    for i in range(10):
        x |= (m & (1 << (2 * i))) >> (2 * i)
        y |= (m & (1 << (2 * i + 1))) >> (2 * i + 1)
        z |= (m & (1 << (2 * i + 2))) >> (2 * i + 2)
    return vec3(x, y, z)
```

## Subtopics

### Triangle-to-Grid Insertion
Triangle-to-Grid Insertion is a simpler method where, for each triangle, the cells overlapped by the triangle's bounding box are determined, and a reference to the triangle is added to each of these cells [S2]. It uses a bounding box overlap test instead of an exact triangle-in-box test. While the exact test reduces triangle references by more than one third, it shrinks ray-triangle intersection tests by only a few percent after mailboxing, making the higher rebuild cost unjustified for most scenes [S2]. However, for scenes with dominantly long, skinny, and diagonal triangles, a more accurate test may still pay off [S2].

## Operating characteristics
*   **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of voxels in the bounding box of each triangle, multiplied by the number of triangles. The 2D cases (4-6) are faster as they iterate over a 2D plane. The 3D cases (7-9) iterate over a 3D volume but use plane tests to skip empty regions [S1, unofficial].
*   **Memory Complexity:** Proportional to the number of intersected voxels. Sparse storage (Morton codes) ensures only occupied voxels are stored [S1, unofficial].
*   **Strengths:** Efficiently handles thin triangles via 2D projection. Robust 3D handling for thick triangles. Compatible with sparse data structures like DAGs/Octrees [S1, unofficial].
*   **Limitations:** Bounding box approximation in the initial step can lead to overestimation of voxels (mitigated by the plane/projection tests). Precision issues may arise with very small `unitlength` or large coordinates [S1, unofficial].
*   **When to use:** When building sparse voxel structures for ray tracing or volume rendering where triangle count is high and geometry varies in thickness [S1, unofficial].

## Background
NGLE Triangle Voxelization is described in the context of building high-resolution Sparse Voxel DAGs [S1, unofficial]. It is part of a pipeline that includes partitioning and octree building. The method is designed to efficiently populate a sparse voxel structure from triangle meshes, leveraging the properties of Morton codes for spatial locality. The approach is detailed in the GitHub repository `leonzheng2/INF584-High_Resolution_Sparse_Voxel_DAGs` [S1, unofficial].
